questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Real-world cross-cloud serverless platforms demand automated image signing and artifact attestations. This question tests end-to-end workflow design, policy enforcement decisions, and practical CI/CD integration skills.

## Key Concepts

- Cosign signing and verification
- Rekor attestations for transparency and auditability
- SBOM generation (using tools like Syft)
- Multi-cloud serverless deployment patterns
- GitHub Actions workflow integration

## Code Example

```yaml
name: cks-serverless-sign
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize]

jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3

      - name: Set up Syft for SBOM
        uses: anchore/syft-action@v1

      - name: Build and push image
        run: |
          docker build -t ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }} .
          docker push ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }}

      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          syft ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }} -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json

      - name: Sign image with cosign
        run: |
          cosign sign --key cosign.key ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }}

      - name: Verify signature
        run: |
          cosign verify --key cosign.pub ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }}

      - name: Upload to Rekor
        run: |
          cosign upload blob -f attestation.json
```

## Failing Manifest (Unsigned Image)

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: serverless-workload
spec:
  containers:
  - name: function
    image: registry.example.com/serverless-fn:abc123
```

## Passing Manifest (Signed Image)

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: serverless-workload
spec:
  containers:
  - name: function
    image: registry.example.com/serverless-fn:signed-sha256
    imagePullPolicy: Always
```

## Local Verification

```bash
# Verify image signature
cosign verify --key cosign.pub registry.example.com/serverless-fn:signed-sha256

# Verify attestation
cosign verify-attestation --type cyclonedx --key cosign.pub registry.example.com/serverless-fn:signed-sha256
```

## CI Verification Steps

1. Add Cosign verification step in CI pipeline
2. Block deployment if signature verification fails
3. Verify SBOM matches image contents
4. Check Rekor transparency log for attestation

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design policy-as-code for multi-cloud Kubernetes with strict residency rules and secret handling. Combines policy design, manifest hardening, and CI validation.

## Key Concepts
- OPA Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- CEL rules for residency checks via namespace and cluster labels
- Kubernetes resourceRequirements and securityContext.runAsNonRoot
- Secrets management with SecretStore/ExternalSecret vs plaintext secrets
- CI verification: kind clusters per cloud, gatekeeper install, policy apply, and test manifests

## Code Example
```javascript
const ct = {
  apiVersion: "templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1",
  kind: "ConstraintTemplate",
  metadata: { name: "k8s_residency" },
  spec: {
    crd: { spec: { names: { Kind: "K8sResidency" } } },
    targets: [{
      target: { kind: "AdmissionReview" },
      code: `package k8s_residency
violation["msg"] {
  ns := input.review.object.metadata.namespace
  residency := input.review.object.metadata.labels["residency"]
  cloud := input.review.review.cloud
  residency != cloud
}`
    }]
  }
}
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest (conceptual)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: app-pass
  namespace: prod
  labels:
    residency: aws
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: app-pass
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: svc
          image: myrepo/app:1.2.3
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "100m"
              memory: "128Mi"
            limits:
              cpu: "500m"
              memory: "256Mi"
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
            runAsUser: 1000
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest (conceptual: residency mismatch / plaintext secret in envFrom)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: app-fail
  namespace: prod
  labels:
    residency: gcp
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: app-fail
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: svc
          image: myrepo/app:0.9.0
          envFrom:
            - secretRef:
                name: my-secret
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "0"
              memory: "0"
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: false
            runAsUser: 0
```

# GitHub Actions: build, sign, verify
name: BuildSignVerify
on: [push]
jobs:
  ci:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Set up QEMU/Buildx

        run: |
          docker buildx create --use

questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Is Asked

This question evaluates a candidate's ability to design production-grade policy gates that enforce artifact provenance and data lineage—critical concerns in multi-cloud ML deployments where governance and compliance are paramount. The question tests practical experience with cryptographic attestation, policy-as-code frameworks, and CI/CD pipeline design.

## Sample OPA Policy

```rego
package data.provenance

default allow = false

allow {
    input.review.kind == "Deployment"
    some i
    input.review.object.spec.template.spec.containers[i].image
    startswith(image, input.config.trusted_registry)
    verify_signature(image)
    tenant_allowed(input.review.namespace)
    lineage_tag_valid(image)
}

verify_signature(image) {
    not missing_signature(image)
    crypto.verify(input.artifacts[image].sig, input.artifacts[image].digest, input.config.public_key)
}

missing_signature(image) {
    not input.artifacts[image]
}

tenant_allowed(ns) {
    input.config.tenant_allowlist[ns]
}

lineage_tag_valid(image) {
    tag := input.artifacts[image].lineage_tag
    input.catalog.tags[tag]
}
```

## Sample Kyverno Policy

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: ml-artifact-provenance
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  rules:
  - name: validate-signed-artifact
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Deployment
    preconditions:
      any:
      - key: '{{ request.namespace }}'
        operator: In
        value: '{{ tenantAllowlist }}'
    validate:
      message: "Artifact must be signed and from trusted registry"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - image: '{{ trustedRegistry }}@*'
      foreach:
      - list: "{{ request.object.spec.template.spec.containers[] }}"
        preconditions:
          all:
          - key: "{{ element.image }}"
            operator: NotIn
            value: [""]
        context:
        - name: artifactData
          apiCall:
            urlPath: "/artifacts/{{ element.image | split("@")[1] }}"
        - name: signatureValid
          apiCall:
            urlPath: "/verify/{{ artifactData.digest }}"
            statement: "$.signature.valid == true"
```

## Failing Manifest Example

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: model-inference
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: inference
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: inference
        image: untrusted-registry.com/models:v1.0  # ❌ Not in trusted registry
        env:
        - name: ARTIFACT_DIGEST
          value: "sha256:abc123"
        - name: LINEAGE_TAG
          value: "raw-data-v2"  # ❌ Tag not in data catalog
```

**Failure Reasons:**
1. Image not from trusted registry
2. Lineage tag `raw-data-v2` not registered in data catalog
3. Missing cryptographic signature
4. Tenant `tenant-a` not in allowlist

## Passing Manifest Example

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: model-inference
  namespace: tenant-a
  annotations:
    artifact.provenance/digest: "sha256:def456"
    artifact.provenance/signature: "LS0tLS1..."
    artifact.provenance/tenant: "tenant-a"
    artifact.provenance/lineage: "processed-features-v1"
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: inference
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: inference
        image: trusted-registry.com/tenant-a/models:v2.1@sha256:def456  # ✓ Trusted registry
        env:
        - name: ARTIFACT_DIGEST
          value: "sha256:def456"
        - name: LINEAGE_TAG
          value: "processed-features-v1"  # ✓ Tag exists in catalog
```

## CI Verification Steps

1. **Extract artifact reference** from deployment manifest
2. **Fetch artifact metadata** from trusted registry API
3. **Validate cryptographic signature** against registry's public key

questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Matters
This tests your ability to design supply chain security for a Kubernetes monorepo where multiple services share base images - a critical skill for CKS certification and real-world cluster security.

## Core Concepts

**Signing vs Attesting:**
- **Signing** (cosign sign): Cryptographically proves an image hasn't been tampered with since it was built and signed
- **Attesting** (cosign attest): Attaches signed metadata (SBOM, provenance) to an image that can be verified later

**SBOM (Software Bill of Materials):**
- Lists all components, packages, and dependencies in an image
- Generated with: `syft image -o spdx-json`
- Standard formats: SPDX, CycloneDX
- Critical for vulnerability scanning and compliance

**SLSA Provenance:**
- Tracks the entire build pipeline (SLSA Level 3+)
- Contains "materials" field that references base image digest
- Enables tracing derived images back to their bases
- Predicate type: `https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1`

**OCI Referrers:**
- Modern way to store attestations alongside images in OCI-compliant registries
- Replaces older annotation-based approaches
- Supported by Harbor, GHCR, ECR, ACR, GCR

**Policy Enforcement:**
- **Kyverno:** Native Kubernetes policy engine with verifyImages rule
- **OPA/Conftest:** General-purpose policy as code
- Run in CI/CD (before `helm upgrade`) AND optionally as admission controllers

**Key Security Properties:**
1. **Base image integrity:** Verify base images are signed and attested
2. **Derivation chain:** Service images must reference an attested base
3. **Immutable records:** Rekor transparency log ensures no retroactive changes
4. **Automated enforcement:** No deployment without verified images

## Code Example
```python
# manifestlint.py
import yaml, sys
ALLOWED_NS = {"dev","staging","prod"}
ALLOWED_REG = {"registry.trusted"}

def ok(manifest):
  docs = yaml.safe_load_all(manifest)
  for m in docs or []:
    if m.get("kind") in {"Deployment","StatefulSet","DaemonSet"}:
      ns = m.get("metadata", {}).get("namespace")
      if ns not in ALLOWED_NS:
        return False
      for c in m.get("spec", {}).get("template", {}).get("spec", {}).get("containers", []):
        img = c.get("image", "")
        if not any(img.startswith(r) for r in ALLOWED_REG) or ":latest" in img:
          return False
  return True

if __name__ == '__main__':
  path = sys.argv[1]
  with open(path) as f:
    print(ok(f.read()))
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to implement scalable, policy-driven security in multi-tenant clusters, with clear tests.

## Key Concepts
- Admission controllers (Kyverno/OPA)
- NetworkPolicy default-deny per namespace
- PodSecurityContext: readOnlyRootFilesystem, capabilities.drop
- Privileged container restrictions and CI checks

## Code Example
```javascript
# Minimal Kyverno policy (YAML shown as JS block for readability)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: enforce-basic-security
spec:
  rules:
  - name: require-psp
    match:
      any:
        - resources:
            kinds: [Namespace, Pod]
    mutate:
      patch: |-
        {"spec": {"securityContext": {"readOnlyRootFilesystem": true, "allowPrivilegeEscalation": false}}}
```
```javascript
# Failing manifest (privileged container)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: bad-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox
    securityContext:
      privileged: true
```
```javascript
# Passing manifest (no privileged, readOnlyRootFilesystem)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: good-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:latest
    securityContext:
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
      capabilities:
        drop: ["ALL"]
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test the policy locally and in CI across multiple namespaces?
- How would you handle exceptions for legacy workloads?
